say.text: Grade II marks inflammation that shows real severity, not the everyday lab line. Think of a much higher count than routine sepsis screens use.
That is not the right choice.
10,000/mm3 is the everyday leucocytosis line on routine labs, so it feels like a severity mark, but TG18 sets a higher count for Grade II.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so check the TG18 list again: Grade II uses its own markers, not the routine lab line.

say.text: TG18 Grade II is any one of four markers: WBC above 18,000/mm3, a palpable tender RUQ mass, complaints over 72 hours, or marked local inflammation.
Routine thresholds such as 10,000/mm3 do not define the grade.
Yes. A WBC above 18,000/mm3 is one of the four Grade II markers, and any one of them is enough.
Now the severe end. Which one finding is enough for TG18 Grade III?

choices.label: Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: Grade III means an organ is failing, not just abnormal. Ask which value is clearly past the line that marks failure, not the one doctors flag on routine reports.
That is not the right choice.
1.5 mg/dL is the familiar kidney warning line from everyday medicine, so it feels like failure, but TG18 counts renal failure only at a higher creatinine.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so separate the familiar kidney warning line from the Grade III renal criterion.

say.text: That is not the right choice.
150,000/mm3 is the routine lower limit on a blood count, so a low platelet feels severe, but TG18 uses a much lower platelet count for Grade III.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so note that a routine platelet limit is not the Grade III platelet criterion.

say.text: Grade III needs organ dysfunction in any one system. Renal dysfunction is creatinine above 2.0 mg/dL or oliguria.
For platelets the line is below 100,000/mm3, far under a routine report.
Yes. Creatinine above 2.0 mg/dL is renal dysfunction, and one failing system is enough for Grade III.

say.text: Grade I is acute cholecystitis that meets neither the Grade II nor the Grade III criteria.
Here WBC is under the 18,000/mm3 line, symptoms are under 72 hours, and creatinine is under 2.0 mg/dL, with no organ failing.
Yes. Neither the Grade II nor the Grade III criteria are met, so this is Grade I, mild.
